hook.en: A library with thousands of books is useless unless they are arranged. By 1865 chemists knew 63 elements and needed a way to arrange them so that their properties made sense.
hook.kn: ಸಾವಿರಾರು ಪುಸ್ತಕಗಳಿರುವ ಗ್ರಂಥಾಲಯ ಜೋಡಿಸದಿದ್ದರೆ ನಿರುಪಯುಕ್ತ. 1865ರ ವೇಳೆಗೆ 63 ಧಾತುಗಳು ತಿಳಿದಿದ್ದವು; ಅವುಗಳ ಗುಣಗಳು ಅರ್ಥವಾಗುವಂತೆ ಜೋಡಿಸುವ ಅಗತ್ಯವಿತ್ತು.

objectives.en: Describe Döbereiner's triads and Newlands' octaves
Explain the merits of Mendeleev's table

narration.en: A library with thousands of books is useless unless they are arranged. By 1865 chemists knew 63 elements and needed a way to arrange them so that their properties made sense.
narration.kn: ಸಾವಿರಾರು ಪುಸ್ತಕಗಳಿರುವ ಗ್ರಂಥಾಲಯ ಜೋಡಿಸದಿದ್ದರೆ ನಿರುಪಯುಕ್ತ. 1865ರ ವೇಳೆಗೆ 63 ಧಾತುಗಳು ತಿಳಿದಿದ್ದವು; ಅವುಗಳ ಗುಣಗಳು ಅರ್ಥವಾಗುವಂತೆ ಜೋಡಿಸುವ ಅಗತ್ಯವಿತ್ತು.

body.en: Döbereiner (1829) grouped similar elements in triads, where the atomic weight of the middle element is about the average of the other two (Li 7, Na 23, K 39). Newlands (1865) arranged elements by increasing atomic weight and noticed that every eighth element resembled the first, like the notes of music: the law of octaves. It worked only up to calcium. Lothar Meyer plotted physical properties against atomic weight and saw periodically repeating patterns.
body.kn: ಡೊಬರೈನರ್ ತ್ರಿಕಗಳು: ಮಧ್ಯದ ಧಾತುವಿನ ಪರಮಾಣು ತೂಕ ಉಳಿದೆರಡರ ಸರಾಸರಿ. ನ್ಯೂಲ್ಯಾಂಡ್ಸ್ ಅಷ್ಟಕ ನಿಯಮ: ಪ್ರತಿ ಎಂಟನೇ ಧಾತು ಮೊದಲನೆಯದನ್ನು ಹೋಲುತ್ತದೆ; ಇದು ಕ್ಯಾಲ್ಸಿಯಂವರೆಗೆ ಮಾತ್ರ ಸರಿ.

points.en: Octaves: valid only up to Ca

narration.en: Döbereiner (1829) grouped similar elements in triads, where the atomic weight of the middle element is about the average of the other two (Li 7, Na 23, K 39). Newlands (1865) arranged elements by increasing atomic weight and noticed that every eighth element resembled the first, like the notes of music: the law of octaves. It worked only up to calcium. Lothar Meyer plotted physical properties against atomic weight and saw periodically repeating patterns.

body.en: Mendeleev (1869): the properties of the elements are a periodic function of their atomic weights. He placed elements in rows and columns by both atomic weight and similar properties, and when the two clashed he trusted the properties. He left gaps for undiscovered elements and predicted their properties: eka-aluminium (gallium) and eka-silicon (germanium) were later found to match closely. He also corrected some atomic weights.
body.kn: ಮೆಂಡಲೀವ್ ಆವರ್ತಕ ನಿಯಮ: ಧಾತುಗಳ ಗುಣಗಳು ಅವುಗಳ ಪರಮಾಣು ತೂಕಗಳ ಆವರ್ತಕ ಫಲನ. ಅವರು ಕಂಡುಹಿಡಿಯದ ಧಾತುಗಳಿಗೆ ಖಾಲಿ ಸ್ಥಾನ ಬಿಟ್ಟು ಅವುಗಳ ಗುಣಗಳನ್ನು ಮುನ್ಸೂಚಿಸಿದರು.

points.en: Gaps left: eka-aluminium = Ga, eka-silicon = Ge
Similar properties given priority over order of weight

problem.en: Show that chlorine, bromine and iodine form a Döbereiner triad (Cl = 35.5, Br = 79.9, I = 126.9).

steps.en: The atomic weight of bromine, 79.9, is close to 81.2, and the three elements have similar properties.

narration.en: Let us solve this together. Show that chlorine, bromine and iodine form a Döbereiner triad (Cl = 35.5, Br = 79.9, I = 126.9).

problem.en: Mendeleev predicted an atomic weight of 72 and a density of 5.5 g cm⁻³ for eka-silicon. Germanium has 72.6 and 5.36 g cm⁻³. What does this show?

steps.en: The predicted and observed values agree within about 1% for atomic weight and 3% for density.
The gaps in his table were real, unknown elements: strong support for the periodic law.

answer.en: His predictions were confirmed, supporting the periodic law
